1	# Step 2 diagnostic sender: design draft
2	
3	Scope: a disposable, isolated selected-case diagnostic only. No production writer, frozen ruler, network call, model response, source reader or automatic decision policy is altered. The preliminary six-pair provider bodies are `shortlist-requests-DRAFT.json` SHA-256 cb142acfe3491dcf6ccfaa70545ffe3c011e3646a2348b36954b04ec2f3321ce; `shortlist-audit-r2.md` audited their construction. The diagnostic seeks to distinguish observed variation in Jev full vs single-question presentation from differences with an independent single-pair model on the same input. It cannot test search recall, group selection, a dispute policy or full-forward effects.
4	
5	**Plan under review, NOT AUTHORIZED TO SEND:** 6 cases × 3 arms × 3 draws = 54 requests, maximum one attempt per request, no retry and no resume. Candidate cases B01, B05, B10, H01, P01, R05 include correct repeat, confirmed wrong-merge and wrong-revision leads, missed repeat and bounded official-denial control. P01 does not show a clearly later forecast revision. R05's stored original-party field conflicts with source attribution. AI blind judgments and source packets are historical diagnostic material, not frozen gold. No hidden scores or Jev answers go into the independent-model body. The order and all exact body bytes must be frozen and independently reviewed before any call. Source packet, reader opinion and matching key hashes, code hashes, per-request body hash, the actual locally adapted DeepSeek body, plus the original Jev full request archive hashes, belong in the manifest. A new output directory must be created exclusively, outside the main live run. Refuse missing/empty inputs, any hash, identity, schema or source mismatch, duplicated case, unsupported arm or configuration.
6	
7	**Draws and costs:** separate one-shot dispatches, each uniquely identified by case, arm, draw; no cache lookups or repeated identifiers. Three draws use identical bodies per arm but distinct persisted attempts. Deterministic shuffled interleaving, seed recorded. Use local repository dated rates, actual bytes and the existing LiveTransport reservation formula; the 54-call reservation is $0.182013 with a 4096 token DeepSeek output cap. Proposed hard reservation $0.25, elapsed limit 1800 s, per-request timeout <=60 s, 54 attempts max. Estimate is not a bill cap. Actual cost and rates must be disclosed; any retries require a separately authorized new diagnostic. More than a few cents requires Alex's explicit instruction under AGENTS §9. The user has not explicitly authorized this 54-request send. Never run beside another paid job, and recheck immediately before a send.
8	
9	**Concurrency**: repo requires pool of 8 for experiment harnesses (AGENTS §9). Before launching a batch, atomically reserve the complete worst-case budget for every request in that batch; persist and fsync dispatching events before launching the batch. At most 8 in flight; every launched request is counted even when delivery is uncertain. The first failure prevents any further batch; all already launched attempts finish or report failure before exit. No automatic retry or restart. Record every launched attempt and response, including those still in flight when failure occurs, and never report an incomplete batch as success. No live database reads. Estimate uses monotonic elapsed time, not calendar to order cases.
10	
11	**Response contract and failure:** Jev must be validated using `jev.validate` for the complete request; only the original target q is compared. DeepSeek receives the prepared adapted JSON bytes exactly once, not re-adapted via LiveTransport; check response JSON, `finish_reason == stop`, refusal field empty, content JSON and `model.check_schema`. Refusal, invalid/missing/extra fields, truncated response, provider error, empty response, timeout, or network reset is failure/unknown delivery; never coerce to a relation or retry silently. A response containing a credential must not be saved. Never print or persist credentials. A process crash after dispatch begins produces an incomplete output; output directory is never resumed. Store raw responses and usage for successful attempts, sanitized failure metadata and available response bytes for failures, immutable actual request bodies, sequence, source hashes and outcome ledger. Partial usage may not reflect charges. Establish uniqueness and atomic durability across threads.
12	
13	**State × event**
14	| State | Event | Response |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| Unprepared | missing inputs, hash mismatch, duplicate ID, disabled provider, missing credential | refuse before any send, report reason without key |
17	| Prepared | other paid work ongoing, no authorization, no preflight, audit outstanding | no live send; independent offline review continues |
18	| Before batch | reservation, call or elapsed cap exceeded | stop without sending batch |
19	| Dispatch | process crash, timeout, unknown delivery | mark incomplete; never resume the directory or assume free |
20	| In flight | any attempt fails or refuses | allow already dispatched batch to settle, record every event, no next batch |
21	| Returned | invalid/truncated/extra data, wrong questions or finish reason | fail and preserve sanitized details; never count as label |
22	| Completed | all 54 unique actual attempts pass schema and identity | preserve full results, blinded source comparison, no product adoption |
23	| Later run | configuration or inputs differ, prior directory exists | refuse; any new run gets new manifest and directory |
24	
25	**Value × reader / new path × checks:** identical body bytes are read by provider, event archive and reviewer; SHA-256 binds all. Original candidate/question identity is read by extraction of Jev target response and audit; wrong identity refuses. DeepSeek output is read by local schema and reviewer; no probability or group rank is invented. Source/reader materials are read only for analysis, never injected into model requests. Usage/cost reservations read by stop guard and report; a missing usage field remains unknown. No product storage, search, model archives or frozen references are modified. The prior Jev path validates all q IDs and shapes; new candidate path must locally validate JSON and finish_reason, with direct actual request-body comparison rather than archive canonical identity. Crash, concurrent failures and duplicate IDs must not silently become success.
26	
27	**Old checks and validation:** offline preflight of relevant archives before any paid send, inspect refusal/skips; compare every original full Jev byte string to historical archive, including question ID and saved answer. Fake-only tests prove each unique job is dispatched once, overlapping in-flight errors cause no subsequent batch, accounting includes in-flight, a malformed JSON, extra key, bad Jev q, refusal, stop reason length, timeout, key echo, hash mismatch, duplicate and missing input fail closed; separately prove the valid control passes. Mutate check on scratch copy to prove a failed response is not accepted. Full request and contract audit by an independent reviewer; print judged-case and fake-attempt counts. Use no key or paid service in tests. No new semantic scorer, no data edits.
28	
29	**Prior decisions:** D381 keeps one most-similar group and member text; D168 includes official denial; PRD §5 deliberately excludes extracted figures from matching; D167 excludes case-fitted rules. No unverified figure, new source context or reinterpretation of these rules enters the requests. A production decision on another comparator, rankings, uncertain outcomes or new reference is not authorized by this design.
30	
31	**Before code:** independent design review; correct every serious finding and re-review. Before sending: separately reviewed source-backed controls including a proper later-forecast revision if broader revision claim is contemplated, frozen cases, full byte audit, offline preflight and fake tests, an independently reviewed sender, current run-state check, then explicit authorization if above few cents. A prior passing rerun does not erase a traced stored error.
32	
33	## Revision 2: response to independent review, supersedes earlier conflicts
34	
35	**Authorization:** Alex replied “开始” on 2026-11-09 in response to the documented three-draw selected-case test, authorizing the 54-request diagnostic within the scope and stated estimate. It does not authorize a forward benchmark, production change or retries. No code or paid send proceeds until the independent design and implementation reviews are clean and the no-cost checks are complete. Estimates are not a guaranteed provider bill ceiling.
36	
37	**Byte transport:** the manifest embeds the six previously audited body strings as immutable UTF-8 bytes with SHA-256 per arm/case, and pins `source-pins-DRAFT.json` (sha256 175a9efa452d1779b6b352e2eee4626acb842a1dcc589e20c1308b0a19422627), each file listed within, selected historical `jev.sqlite` request SHA/answer and source mapping, code and settings digests. A coordinator validates all 18 bodies against their pins and original historic Jev archives before any live call. The child makes exactly one `urllib.request.Request(..., data=body_bytes, ...)` using those bytes; no parsing/reserialization, `jev.transport`, `jev.ask`, `model.call`, default retry, or archive lookup. HTTP 429, reset, timeout and any ambiguous delivery stop the line; there are no retries or resumption. Each draw has a distinct job ID but identical provider bytes. Captured raw fake HTTP must equal each registered byte string; distinct dispatches do not prove provider-side statistical independence.
38	
39	**Ownership and concurrency:** one coordinator exclusively creates a new run directory with `mkdir(exist_ok=False)`, writes and fsyncs its immutable manifest and plan, and fsyncs the parent directory. Other process or existing scope cannot write or resume it. The coordinator owns the ordered ledger, reservation and process lifecycle. It dispatches fixed batches of at most 8 independently launched child processes. Before creating any child, it reserves every job in that batch, durably writes `may_have_been_sent` for each including sequence, request hash and reserved amount, and fsyncs; this is intentionally conservative if the parent crashes before submission. A single worker owns exactly one HTTP invocation, hands only a sanitized result to its parent, and does not write the run directory. If process creation or ledger persistence fails, the batch's unresolved jobs remain unknown, no further batch is submitted, and a failed ledger is never represented as a complete run. Failure in one child prevents the next batch; all already submitted workers are collected, or terminated at the deadline and marked unknown. The coordinator writes results and fsyncs, then an exclusive terminal record only after all 54 unique jobs have successful validated responses. It refuses any in-flight work, missing responses, failed output write, simultaneous writer, changed input or mismatched plan. A crash is permanently incomplete with no automatic retry, even if the request might never have left.
40	
41	**Timeout and budget:** use frozen explicit dated rate inputs for Jev (.042 USD/million input; zero output in repository table) and DeepSeek (.30/1.20 USD/million); reserve per job `(2 * len(body_bytes) + 4096) * input_rate / 1e6 + output_cap * output_rate / 1e6`. Whole diagnostic reservation <= $0.25 and 54 invocations; no reservation is released for failed, unknown or completed attempts. This is a conservative operational estimate, not a mathematically guaranteed token ceiling or a provider bill cap. Coordinator uses monotonic elapsed, a 1,800 s deadline, and passes each child `min(60 s, remaining)`; child process provides process-level bound rather than trusting socket timeout. At deadline the coordinator terminates live children, records unknown delivery and refuses success. Record count/reservation before invocation, not after successful responses. Fake clock and deliberately blocked fake child test limits, in-flight accounting, termination and refusal to continue.
42	
43	**Secret and response boundary:** keys are loaded by live child only, using existing provider key readers; no key in argv, logs, manifest, or exception. Before any raw response is persisted, encoded, parsed into a diagnostic or sent over IPC, compare bytes against credential encodings (raw UTF-8, base64 and URL-escaped); on any match discard entire body and report only `secret_echo`. HTTP error bodies are discarded and only an allowlisted status/failure class is returned; never log arbitrary exception text, tracebacks, headers or error body. Successful response bytes may only be retained after credential checks and strict validation. Test fake credentials in success, malformed/error and encoded responses and scan the entire output for each fake secret. If success body is untrusted and cannot be safely verified as secret-free, it is discarded, not archived.
44	
45	**Closed accepted responses:** parse UTF-8 JSON with `object_pairs_hook` rejecting duplicate keys and `parse_constant` rejecting NaN/Infinity. Jev envelope is an object with exactly model, answers and usage as observed in saved responses; model must be the requested Jev ID; `answers` has exactly requested question IDs, each choice object has exact fields `type`, `choice`, `confidence`, `probabilities`, with choice and probability keys matching exactly the question criteria, finite confidence in [0,1], and `jev.validate` must return no problems. Usage is an object; token fields, when present, are nonnegative integers (not booleans), and absent usage is unknown, not zero cost. DeepSeek response envelope is object containing `model`, `choices` and optionally provider metadata; reject non-object, missing model or choices, wrong model, non-list or not exactly one choice; require choice `finish_reason` exactly `stop`, message object, assistant role, content string, and refusal absent or null; strict JSON-parse content then validate the exact frozen schema (`choice` only, enum different/same_statement/supersedes, no extra keys) using `model.check_schema`. Provider-added metadata fields are not treated as labels. Usage tokens are nonnegative ints when present; missing is unknown. Unknown JSON envelope, output truncation or refusal is failure, never `different`. Check actual provider contracts and stored response envelopes before an implementation chooses strictness; the local validator is only used for its supported simple object subset, not general JSON Schema.
46	
47	**Explicit state × event:**
48	| State | Event | Durable transition and time basis |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| not created | missing input, mismatched pin, duplicate ID, missing key, preflight skips/refuses | refuse before directory or call; report safe class; historical source dates untouched |
51	| prepared | competing run or mismatch after wait | no call; reverify all pins and process state immediately before dispatch |
52	| directory created | competing writer or existing name | exclusive mkdir refuses; never merge or resume outputs |
53	| batch planned | cap or deadline fails | no submission; persist safe `not_dispatched` terminal if possible; monotonic clock |
54	| reserved | crash before worker creation or during submission | pre-fsynced `may_have_been_sent` remains unknown; no retry; monotonic sequence preserved |
55	| in flight | one worker fails, refusal, invalid JSON, secret or HTTP failure | stop after this batch, collect others; sanitized event per worker; no next batch |
56	| in flight | deadline, child hangs or coordinator crash | terminate child at deadline, unknown delivery and reserved cost; no final success; no retry |
57	| in flight | input corrected or config changed | manifest already pins body; detect mismatch before each batch, stop and require a new design/run |
58	| result ready | ledger or fsync fails | stop and report incomplete; never infer completion from in-memory result |
59	| returned | usage missing, provider rate unknown | usage unknown; never fabricate cost; configured reservation retained |
60	| terminal | 54 unique valid attempts plus no in flight | fsync complete marker and directory; analysis labels remain diagnostic, never product writes |
61	| later | attempted resume, different scope or later date | exclusive directory refusal; new manifest and path, source dates unchanged |
62	
63	**Value × reader table:**
64	| Value/writer | Every reader | Contract |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| registered body bytes / preparation | provider, fake HTTP capture, ledger, auditor | exact SHA, original candidate/q, no adapter applied twice |
67	| source IDs / preparation | independent source reviewers, audit only | complete saved article and source spans; never included in model comparison unless already in piece text |
68	| blind opinions / readers | analyst and independent reviewer | frozen AI opinions, disputed separately; never sent as prompts or called gold |
69	| per-job key and reservation / coordinator | scheduler, durable ledger, cost report | unique, pre-reserved, no release on unknown; timestamps do not order |
70	| raw provider response / child | strict validator only before release | credential scan first; errors and unsafe content discarded |
71	| sanitized validated response / child | coordinator and human trace reader | fail on unknown, no new labels or inferred probability |
72	| partial/completed result / coordinator | human, independent council | only 54 valid unique responses count complete; preserve unknown/failures |
73	
74	**New path × old checks:**
75	| Check | Jev full | Jev one question | Independent model |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| historic input | full byte-equal archived control, question ID/answer checked | target is same question/state/ID | exact same pair text and definitions; provider/format changes disclosed |
78	| accepted response | strict envelope plus existing `jev.validate` for all q | same for one q | strict envelope, finish/refusal and local three-label schema |
79	| no cached draws | 54 distinct one-shot fake HTTP jobs | same | same |
80	| time/cost/attempt limits | all reserved before batch, one HTTP per job | same | same incl 4096 output cap |
81	| failed answer | sanitized failure or unknown, no label | same | same |
82	| frozen source and product | no edits; AI source opinions not ruler | same | same |
83	
84	**Six-case diagnostic and falsifiers:** B01 valid repeat; B05 wrong update; B10 wrong merge; H01 missed repeat; R05 wrong update with known party-attribution conflict; P01 direct denial control with known date/old-article caveat. This revises the earlier 12-pair exploration; B06/H02, later chronological revisions and unclear cases remain deferred. Fix reference opinions and source packet hashes before any fresh answer. All three draws must be separately dispatched. Compare fresh Jev full against fresh Jev single before attributing any change to a provider. Claim a repeatable selected-case signal only for source-supported wrong cases corrected by the independent model in at least 2/3 draws where the fresh Jev control misses at least 2/3, with B01/P01 maintained; report all regressions, failure, uncertainty and cost first. If Jev baseline fails its own source-backed controls in 2/3 draws, or candidate loses B01/P01 in 2/3, stop and trace. A passing rerun does not erase a stored error. No global quality, calibrated probability, group-rank, or end-to-end claim follows.
85	
86	**Check controls and mutations:** exercise actual command entry with 54 fake attempts; code paths and variants (bad body SHA, duplicate jobs, bad archive/q, missing input, malformed JSON, duplicate keys, NaN, bad Jev answer set/probabilities, wrong model, DeepSeek truncation/refusal/extra label, 429/reset/timeout, echo secret, launch failure, log failure, mid-batch concurrent failures, blocked worker/deadline, missing usage, pre-existing output directory) must each be deliberately exercised with explicit positive control, judged counts and scratch-only artifacts. Mutate each core check on scratch copy so its negative control goes red. Compare fake-captured outgoing body bytes to registered strings and show exactly one fake invocation per submitted attempt. No real key access allowed in fake controls. Before paid calls run `scripts/preflight.py` with explicitly named completed saved archives/views, read skips and refusals, and independent audit of all request text, standard and schema. If existing preflight cannot cover this clean Step 2 path, state it, and additionally replay the exact archived control identity and saved responses through the current checks at $0; do not infer coverage it does not have. Any semantic judgment is source-reviewed by humans/independent readers, not a new scorer.
87	
88	## Revision 3: concrete answers to review round 2
89	
90	**Execution and process death:** replace child processes with one actual OS process containing a fixed pool of at most eight worker threads. The coordinator is the only writer and pre-fsyncs all batch `may_have_been_sent` entries before submitting any worker. A process termination ends all its threads, so no child process can outlive it; the remote provider can still have received a request, and all nonterminal reserved attempts remain unknown, never presumed unsent or unbilled. Each batch has an absolute monotonic deadline `min(global_deadline, batch_start+60)`. Use `concurrent.futures.wait` with that deadline. At deadline, the coordinator persists safe terminal incomplete events for all unfinished jobs and fsyncs, then forcibly terminates its own diagnostic process (`os._exit` in CLI only); OS closes all sockets and stops threads. This does not guarantee a remote request was canceled. If the machine/OS fails before fsync, absence of a terminal marker still means incomplete. A separate subprocess-based fake test kills the *actual coordinator* during blocked fake HTTP, asserts it exits, has no descendant processes, leaves only unknown in-flight records, never resumes, and its test-owned fake server receives no new connections after termination. A socket timeout is defense in depth, not the whole-response deadline. The user authorized this bounded 54-request diagnostic in their latest “开始”; no new approval needed for that same scope.
91	
92	**Redirect and exact HTTP:** workers use an opener containing an explicit no-redirect handler and one `open` on the fixed official HTTPS endpoint. Statuses in the 3xx range are failures and never followed. The opener cannot delegate to `jev.transport` or default `openai_transport`. A local fake HTTP server captures and counts actual calls, including a 302 with a second target, 429, socket reset and Unicode/key-order cases: exactly one invocation, zero second-target requests, body bytes equal pinned bytes. The coordinator does not send credentials to any URL from a response.
93	
94	**Bounded response and secret boundary:** reject any declared Content-Length above 2 MiB and read incrementally up to 2 MiB+1. Require full EOF and exact Content-Length when provided; oversize, premature EOF and read errors discard body and fail. With no Content-Length, EOF ends the bounded response; malformed JSON cannot pass. Worker scans raw bytes for credential raw/base64/URL forms, strict parses in memory, then recursively scans every decoded object string, including JSON-unescaped strings, again for all these forms before passing or persisting anything. Error status bodies and all traceback/headers/arbitrary exceptions are always discarded without entering IPC or logs; failure record only enum and numeric status. Successful validated sanitized bodies may be archived, with any serialization after decoded scan also scanned. Fake secrets in raw, JSON escaped, base64 and URL-escaped responses, headers, HTTP error and malformed body must not appear in any file, log or IPC. No real credentials are loaded in fake tests. Provider reported usage JSON is retained with validated safe response; DeepSeek reasoning tokens are a subset of completion tokens, never double-billed. Missing usage is unknown rather than a zero charge.
95	
96	**Closed provider response contracts:** all JSON parsers reject duplicate object keys, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8. Jev archived validation found 206/206 fresh and 590/590 D392 top-level envelopes exactly `model, answers, usage`, model `jev-1.14.0`; the selected choice answers carry exactly `type, choice, confidence, probabilities`. For this research diagnostic accept only that envelope with model exact, choice field sets exactly as above, real non-bool finite numeric confidence, existing `jev.validate` for every requested question, and `usage` an object; token fields, when present, are non-bool nonnegative integers; missing token fields become unknown. DeepSeek archived validation found 193/193 c8 responses model `deepseek-flash` and standard response metadata; live provider output must be an object with keys from `{id,object,created,model,choices,usage,system_fingerprint}` with required `model,choices`; optional metadata must have their standard types (id/object/fingerprint string or null as appropriate; created integer, not bool; usage object). Require one choice, index zero if present, finish_reason `stop`, message `role=assistant`, non-null string content, refusal absent/null; permit `reasoning_content` string/null and standard optional choice `logprobs`; reject unknown fields in choices or message and any second choice. Strict parse the content, then check the exact three-label schema and reject extra/missing fields. This is a conservative probe contract: actual provider variants that do not match are refusals, never force-fitted. Before paid send positive controls use saved Jev and DeepSeek provider response envelopes (the archive-only `sent_request` field is removed only from the *response control*, never from a request), and a conforming synthetic choice answer. A schema failure in a real previously accepted stored control stops investigation rather than silently loosening validation.
97	
98	**Evidence chain:** `evidence-chain-DRAFT.json` SHA-256 6b0ab060329917c7bfb7c21648b611f4a856e1c99cac8f43b051c7225ce07146 maps each selected ID to an explicit completed historic archive path and archive SHA, exact full Jev request SHA, original question ID and historic target-answer SHA, source packet/file and incoming/stored source IDs, canonical per-source article SHA, source-opinion and all provider body hashes. `source-pins-DRAFT.json` SHA-256 175a9efa452d1779b6b352e2eee4626acb842a1dcc589e20c1308b0a19422627 pins all 13 complete source and independent-review files. Read no live database; check sqlite URI `mode=ro`, recompute archive file hash before and after archive verification, check `request_json` byte identity and original target answer for each case; fail if archive changes or missing. Explicitly verify the record's quoted passages occur in or are flagged as unverified against corresponding source text; never infer that numerical metadata is supported just by occurrence. Prior source opinions remain provisional and R05 attribution/P01 timing caveats follow the case.
99	
100	**Result rule:** report each 3-answer row for each arm and every transport/schema/usage failure, no scorer. B01 is expected same and P01 supersedes; each must be selected in >=2/3 fresh Jev-full draws for the diagnostic to support any improvement claim, and >=2/3 independent draws to avoid a repeatable regression. If either fresh Jev-full baseline control fails this condition, stop interpretation and trace. If Jev single and full disagree on a selected relation >=2/3 vs <=1/3, disclose that as request-shape sensitivity and use Jev single for the same-input model comparison, while retaining full results separately; never assign effect solely to model. For B05/B10/H01/R05, a selected-case improvement requires independent correct >=2/3 and fresh Jev-single correct <=1/3 on at least one, with zero repeatable regression on B01/P01; otherwise stop or report inconclusive. One draw does not establish repeatability. P01 only covers direct-denial link, not later forecast changes, and R05 has conflicting party attribution. No global precision/recall, group ranking, model causality or downstream claim.
101	
102	**Additional fake checks:** include redirect to credential-capturing second server, 2 MiB limit and incomplete Content-Length, all decoded-secret encodings, end-to-end process SIGKILL and timeout with eight blocked fake workers, no orphans, unknown-delivery ledger, no dispatch beyond a failing batch, exclusive scope, source/artifact byte mismatch, no provider-model alias coercion, valid real archived envelope controls, usage absent and invalid. Every check has a positive test and targeted mutant, actual CLI path, judged nonzero sample, no real credentials/services. Preflight baseline run `preflight-v108.log` exited 0 on explicit completed v108 d1: 243 extraction answers; 726 entries judged/12 rejected (7 quote mismatch, 5 duplicate quote); 170 matching judgments, 2 skipped because request absent; 2 earlier schema-refused rows. This matches the earlier score experiment's reported 243/170 and 2 skipped; it does not replay clean Step 2. Explicitly reconstruct and validate all six saved Jev requests and answer shapes separately, plus the selected source/reader opinions; do not claim v108 preflight covers clean Jev or clean c8.
103	
104	Source-span audit detail: 20 of 21 selected record passages occur byte-for-byte in their saved source article text; R05's stored retailer passage contains a single space where the saved source has a newline between sentences. It matches after collapsing whitespace only. Preserve and report that normalization; do not call it a byte-exact quotation or treat it as a content contradiction. This audit concerns supplied saved source and does not independently validate the upstream article or record attribution.
105	
106	## Revision 4: eliminate arbitrary retained response text
107	
108	The diagnostic does not need model reasoning, free-form metadata, IDs, timestamps, provider-generated strings or raw response text. After the raw-byte check, a strict parse, and recursive scanning of all decoded keys and values for the credential and common encodings, the worker returns only a newly constructed **allowlisted structured result**: fixed case/arm/draw identifiers from the manifest; for Jev, the target question ID from the manifest and for every required question only the fixed enum choice and finite numerical confidence/probabilities indexed by the three fixed manifest labels; for DeepSeek, only the fixed enum choice; and for either provider only recognized numeric token usage fields and safe numeric HTTP status. Model `reasoning_content`, generated metadata, arbitrary strings, original content and raw HTTP body are always discarded, even on a successful response. Every retained string is either a fixed local identifier/enum or comes from a fixed question/criterion in the validated request; the serialized allowlist result is checked for credential raw/base64/URL forms before IPC or persistence. Decoded object keys as well as values are scanned. Thus nested JSON or escape sequences in discarded arbitrary response strings can never leave the worker; decoded JSON inside DeepSeek content is itself strict parsed and has only a constrained enum. No arbitrary exception message or error body is retained. Add a fake response with doubly encoded secret in `reasoning_content`, another in response metadata/object keys, and assert no secret or its encoding appears anywhere in IPC, logs or saved files; mutate the allowlist to retain arbitrary fields and prove the test fails. The tradeoff is that raw reasoning and arbitrary successful provider response metadata are not archived; local typed answers, actual input bytes and usage suffice for this probe's comparison, and response refusals are reported only by safe failure type.
109	
110	## Implementation note: single-process credentials and live-run gate
111	
112	The coordinator and workers are threads in one process; `main` reads both credentials after the review, preflight and process-state gates and passes them in memory to worker threads. There is no separate worker process or isolated worker address space; the earlier statement that only a child reads keys is superseded. They never enter argv, plan, manifest, event log or fake tests, and safe failure records discard response/error text. Exact key access and gate ordering are subject to the independent sender review. The run-state gate can identify known repository launch commands and repeats immediately before dispatch and every batch; it cannot prove no unrelated process anywhere on the machine makes a paid model call, so the operator also checks known active jobs immediately before send. The complete unmodified v108 preflight output is compared byte-for-byte with the dated baseline, saved alongside the probe, and its two schema-refused, 12 extraction-dropped and two skipped records are disclosed; clean Step 2 still uses the separate six-case stored-answer replay, not that preflight.
113	
114	The completed D392 stage-2 run is recorded in main commit 9552c8d. For the positive DeepSeek envelope control, a single completed historical archive response was extracted once from d1 segment 2, call_id 1 (source response SHA-256 b44933a35e944cabae3c9bcb43bc8430cc7fa4b43a70906bfcacac21489d4e3e; completed source database SHA-256 e5a182b517ef63431d2501ce8f9268c92f527cf0d71d758efb77e6ef73695005). The archived-only request field was removed and the content replaced with a synthetic three-choice response; free-form reasoning was set to null. The sanitized `deepseek-envelope-control.json` SHA-256 ccce7ed50966b0461a3bb56fc8023481fecc6789ff37631884f7b4a134cf2ec0 is checked directly during dispatch preparation; the live sender does not open that historical trace database.
115

# Step 2 diagnostic sender: design draft

Scope: a disposable, isolated selected-case diagnostic only. No production writer, frozen ruler, network call, model response, source reader or automatic decision policy is altered. The preliminary six-pair provider bodies are `shortlist-requests-DRAFT.json` SHA-256 cb142acfe3491dcf6ccfaa70545ffe3c011e3646a2348b36954b04ec2f3321ce; `shortlist-audit-r2.md` audited their construction. The diagnostic seeks to distinguish observed variation in Jev full vs single-question presentation from differences with an independent single-pair model on the same input. It cannot test search recall, group selection, a dispute policy or full-forward effects.

**Plan under review, NOT AUTHORIZED TO SEND:** 6 cases × 3 arms × 3 draws = 54 requests, maximum one attempt per request, no retry and no resume. Candidate cases B01, B05, B10, H01, P01, R05 include correct repeat, confirmed wrong-merge and wrong-revision leads, missed repeat and bounded official-denial control. P01 does not show a clearly later forecast revision. R05's stored original-party field conflicts with source attribution. AI blind judgments and source packets are historical diagnostic material, not frozen gold. No hidden scores or Jev answers go into the independent-model body. The order and all exact body bytes must be frozen and independently reviewed before any call. Source packet, reader opinion and matching key hashes, code hashes, per-request body hash, the actual locally adapted DeepSeek body, plus the original Jev full request archive hashes, belong in the manifest. A new output directory must be created exclusively, outside the main live run. Refuse missing/empty inputs, any hash, identity, schema or source mismatch, duplicated case, unsupported arm or configuration.

**Draws and costs:** separate one-shot dispatches, each uniquely identified by case, arm, draw; no cache lookups or repeated identifiers. Three draws use identical bodies per arm but distinct persisted attempts. Deterministic shuffled interleaving, seed recorded. Use local repository dated rates, actual bytes and the existing LiveTransport reservation formula; the 54-call reservation is $0.182013 with a 4096 token DeepSeek output cap. Proposed hard reservation $0.25, elapsed limit 1800 s, per-request timeout <=60 s, 54 attempts max. Estimate is not a bill cap. Actual cost and rates must be disclosed; any retries require a separately authorized new diagnostic. More than a few cents requires Alex's explicit instruction under AGENTS §9. The user has not explicitly authorized this 54-request send. Never run beside another paid job, and recheck immediately before a send.

**Concurrency**: repo requires pool of 8 for experiment harnesses (AGENTS §9). Before launching a batch, atomically reserve the complete worst-case budget for every request in that batch; persist and fsync dispatching events before launching the batch. At most 8 in flight; every launched request is counted even when delivery is uncertain. The first failure prevents any further batch; all already launched attempts finish or report failure before exit. No automatic retry or restart. Record every launched attempt and response, including those still in flight when failure occurs, and never report an incomplete batch as success. No live database reads. Estimate uses monotonic elapsed time, not calendar to order cases.

**Response contract and failure:** Jev must be validated using `jev.validate` for the complete request; only the original target q is compared. DeepSeek receives the prepared adapted JSON bytes exactly once, not re-adapted via LiveTransport; check response JSON, `finish_reason == stop`, refusal field empty, content JSON and `model.check_schema`. Refusal, invalid/missing/extra fields, truncated response, provider error, empty response, timeout, or network reset is failure/unknown delivery; never coerce to a relation or retry silently. A response containing a credential must not be saved. Never print or persist credentials. A process crash after dispatch begins produces an incomplete output; output directory is never resumed. Store raw responses and usage for successful attempts, sanitized failure metadata and available response bytes for failures, immutable actual request bodies, sequence, source hashes and outcome ledger. Partial usage may not reflect charges. Establish uniqueness and atomic durability across threads.

**State × event**
| State | Event | Response |
|---|---|---|
| Unprepared | missing inputs, hash mismatch, duplicate ID, disabled provider, missing credential | refuse before any send, report reason without key |
| Prepared | other paid work ongoing, no authorization, no preflight, audit outstanding | no live send; independent offline review continues |
| Before batch | reservation, call or elapsed cap exceeded | stop without sending batch |
| Dispatch | process crash, timeout, unknown delivery | mark incomplete; never resume the directory or assume free |
| In flight | any attempt fails or refuses | allow already dispatched batch to settle, record every event, no next batch |
| Returned | invalid/truncated/extra data, wrong questions or finish reason | fail and preserve sanitized details; never count as label |
| Completed | all 54 unique actual attempts pass schema and identity | preserve full results, blinded source comparison, no product adoption |
| Later run | configuration or inputs differ, prior directory exists | refuse; any new run gets new manifest and directory |

**Value × reader / new path × checks:** identical body bytes are read by provider, event archive and reviewer; SHA-256 binds all. Original candidate/question identity is read by extraction of Jev target response and audit; wrong identity refuses. DeepSeek output is read by local schema and reviewer; no probability or group rank is invented. Source/reader materials are read only for analysis, never injected into model requests. Usage/cost reservations read by stop guard and report; a missing usage field remains unknown. No product storage, search, model archives or frozen references are modified. The prior Jev path validates all q IDs and shapes; new candidate path must locally validate JSON and finish_reason, with direct actual request-body comparison rather than archive canonical identity. Crash, concurrent failures and duplicate IDs must not silently become success.

**Old checks and validation:** offline preflight of relevant archives before any paid send, inspect refusal/skips; compare every original full Jev byte string to historical archive, including question ID and saved answer. Fake-only tests prove each unique job is dispatched once, overlapping in-flight errors cause no subsequent batch, accounting includes in-flight, a malformed JSON, extra key, bad Jev q, refusal, stop reason length, timeout, key echo, hash mismatch, duplicate and missing input fail closed; separately prove the valid control passes. Mutate check on scratch copy to prove a failed response is not accepted. Full request and contract audit by an independent reviewer; print judged-case and fake-attempt counts. Use no key or paid service in tests. No new semantic scorer, no data edits.

**Prior decisions:** D381 keeps one most-similar group and member text; D168 includes official denial; PRD §5 deliberately excludes extracted figures from matching; D167 excludes case-fitted rules. No unverified figure, new source context or reinterpretation of these rules enters the requests. A production decision on another comparator, rankings, uncertain outcomes or new reference is not authorized by this design.

**Before code:** independent design review; correct every serious finding and re-review. Before sending: separately reviewed source-backed controls including a proper later-forecast revision if broader revision claim is contemplated, frozen cases, full byte audit, offline preflight and fake tests, an independently reviewed sender, current run-state check, then explicit authorization if above few cents. A prior passing rerun does not erase a traced stored error.

## Revision 2: response to independent review, supersedes earlier conflicts

**Authorization:** Alex replied “开始” on 2026-11-09 in response to the documented three-draw selected-case test, authorizing the 54-request diagnostic within the scope and stated estimate. It does not authorize a forward benchmark, production change or retries. No code or paid send proceeds until the independent design and implementation reviews are clean and the no-cost checks are complete. Estimates are not a guaranteed provider bill ceiling.

**Byte transport:** the manifest embeds the six previously audited body strings as immutable UTF-8 bytes with SHA-256 per arm/case, and pins `source-pins-DRAFT.json` (sha256 175a9efa452d1779b6b352e2eee4626acb842a1dcc589e20c1308b0a19422627), each file listed within, selected historical `jev.sqlite` request SHA/answer and source mapping, code and settings digests. A coordinator validates all 18 bodies against their pins and original historic Jev archives before any live call. The child makes exactly one `urllib.request.Request(..., data=body_bytes, ...)` using those bytes; no parsing/reserialization, `jev.transport`, `jev.ask`, `model.call`, default retry, or archive lookup. HTTP 429, reset, timeout and any ambiguous delivery stop the line; there are no retries or resumption. Each draw has a distinct job ID but identical provider bytes. Captured raw fake HTTP must equal each registered byte string; distinct dispatches do not prove provider-side statistical independence.

**Ownership and concurrency:** one coordinator exclusively creates a new run directory with `mkdir(exist_ok=False)`, writes and fsyncs its immutable manifest and plan, and fsyncs the parent directory. Other process or existing scope cannot write or resume it. The coordinator owns the ordered ledger, reservation and process lifecycle. It dispatches fixed batches of at most 8 independently launched child processes. Before creating any child, it reserves every job in that batch, durably writes `may_have_been_sent` for each including sequence, request hash and reserved amount, and fsyncs; this is intentionally conservative if the parent crashes before submission. A single worker owns exactly one HTTP invocation, hands only a sanitized result to its parent, and does not write the run directory. If process creation or ledger persistence fails, the batch's unresolved jobs remain unknown, no further batch is submitted, and a failed ledger is never represented as a complete run. Failure in one child prevents the next batch; all already submitted workers are collected, or terminated at the deadline and marked unknown. The coordinator writes results and fsyncs, then an exclusive terminal record only after all 54 unique jobs have successful validated responses. It refuses any in-flight work, missing responses, failed output write, simultaneous writer, changed input or mismatched plan. A crash is permanently incomplete with no automatic retry, even if the request might never have left.

**Timeout and budget:** use frozen explicit dated rate inputs for Jev (.042 USD/million input; zero output in repository table) and DeepSeek (.30/1.20 USD/million); reserve per job `(2 * len(body_bytes) + 4096) * input_rate / 1e6 + output_cap * output_rate / 1e6`. Whole diagnostic reservation <= $0.25 and 54 invocations; no reservation is released for failed, unknown or completed attempts. This is a conservative operational estimate, not a mathematically guaranteed token ceiling or a provider bill cap. Coordinator uses monotonic elapsed, a 1,800 s deadline, and passes each child `min(60 s, remaining)`; child process provides process-level bound rather than trusting socket timeout. At deadline the coordinator terminates live children, records unknown delivery and refuses success. Record count/reservation before invocation, not after successful responses. Fake clock and deliberately blocked fake child test limits, in-flight accounting, termination and refusal to continue.

**Secret and response boundary:** keys are loaded by live child only, using existing provider key readers; no key in argv, logs, manifest, or exception. Before any raw response is persisted, encoded, parsed into a diagnostic or sent over IPC, compare bytes against credential encodings (raw UTF-8, base64 and URL-escaped); on any match discard entire body and report only `secret_echo`. HTTP error bodies are discarded and only an allowlisted status/failure class is returned; never log arbitrary exception text, tracebacks, headers or error body. Successful response bytes may only be retained after credential checks and strict validation. Test fake credentials in success, malformed/error and encoded responses and scan the entire output for each fake secret. If success body is untrusted and cannot be safely verified as secret-free, it is discarded, not archived.

**Closed accepted responses:** parse UTF-8 JSON with `object_pairs_hook` rejecting duplicate keys and `parse_constant` rejecting NaN/Infinity. Jev envelope is an object with exactly model, answers and usage as observed in saved responses; model must be the requested Jev ID; `answers` has exactly requested question IDs, each choice object has exact fields `type`, `choice`, `confidence`, `probabilities`, with choice and probability keys matching exactly the question criteria, finite confidence in [0,1], and `jev.validate` must return no problems. Usage is an object; token fields, when present, are nonnegative integers (not booleans), and absent usage is unknown, not zero cost. DeepSeek response envelope is object containing `model`, `choices` and optionally provider metadata; reject non-object, missing model or choices, wrong model, non-list or not exactly one choice; require choice `finish_reason` exactly `stop`, message object, assistant role, content string, and refusal absent or null; strict JSON-parse content then validate the exact frozen schema (`choice` only, enum different/same_statement/supersedes, no extra keys) using `model.check_schema`. Provider-added metadata fields are not treated as labels. Usage tokens are nonnegative ints when present; missing is unknown. Unknown JSON envelope, output truncation or refusal is failure, never `different`. Check actual provider contracts and stored response envelopes before an implementation chooses strictness; the local validator is only used for its supported simple object subset, not general JSON Schema.

**Explicit state × event:**
| State | Event | Durable transition and time basis |
|---|---|---|
| not created | missing input, mismatched pin, duplicate ID, missing key, preflight skips/refuses | refuse before directory or call; report safe class; historical source dates untouched |
| prepared | competing run or mismatch after wait | no call; reverify all pins and process state immediately before dispatch |
| directory created | competing writer or existing name | exclusive mkdir refuses; never merge or resume outputs |
| batch planned | cap or deadline fails | no submission; persist safe `not_dispatched` terminal if possible; monotonic clock |
| reserved | crash before worker creation or during submission | pre-fsynced `may_have_been_sent` remains unknown; no retry; monotonic sequence preserved |
| in flight | one worker fails, refusal, invalid JSON, secret or HTTP failure | stop after this batch, collect others; sanitized event per worker; no next batch |
| in flight | deadline, child hangs or coordinator crash | terminate child at deadline, unknown delivery and reserved cost; no final success; no retry |
| in flight | input corrected or config changed | manifest already pins body; detect mismatch before each batch, stop and require a new design/run |
| result ready | ledger or fsync fails | stop and report incomplete; never infer completion from in-memory result |
| returned | usage missing, provider rate unknown | usage unknown; never fabricate cost; configured reservation retained |
| terminal | 54 unique valid attempts plus no in flight | fsync complete marker and directory; analysis labels remain diagnostic, never product writes |
| later | attempted resume, different scope or later date | exclusive directory refusal; new manifest and path, source dates unchanged |

**Value × reader table:**
| Value/writer | Every reader | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| registered body bytes / preparation | provider, fake HTTP capture, ledger, auditor | exact SHA, original candidate/q, no adapter applied twice |
| source IDs / preparation | independent source reviewers, audit only | complete saved article and source spans; never included in model comparison unless already in piece text |
| blind opinions / readers | analyst and independent reviewer | frozen AI opinions, disputed separately; never sent as prompts or called gold |
| per-job key and reservation / coordinator | scheduler, durable ledger, cost report | unique, pre-reserved, no release on unknown; timestamps do not order |
| raw provider response / child | strict validator only before release | credential scan first; errors and unsafe content discarded |
| sanitized validated response / child | coordinator and human trace reader | fail on unknown, no new labels or inferred probability |
| partial/completed result / coordinator | human, independent council | only 54 valid unique responses count complete; preserve unknown/failures |

**New path × old checks:**
| Check | Jev full | Jev one question | Independent model |
|---|---|---|---|
| historic input | full byte-equal archived control, question ID/answer checked | target is same question/state/ID | exact same pair text and definitions; provider/format changes disclosed |
| accepted response | strict envelope plus existing `jev.validate` for all q | same for one q | strict envelope, finish/refusal and local three-label schema |
| no cached draws | 54 distinct one-shot fake HTTP jobs | same | same |
| time/cost/attempt limits | all reserved before batch, one HTTP per job | same | same incl 4096 output cap |
| failed answer | sanitized failure or unknown, no label | same | same |
| frozen source and product | no edits; AI source opinions not ruler | same | same |

**Six-case diagnostic and falsifiers:** B01 valid repeat; B05 wrong update; B10 wrong merge; H01 missed repeat; R05 wrong update with known party-attribution conflict; P01 direct denial control with known date/old-article caveat. This revises the earlier 12-pair exploration; B06/H02, later chronological revisions and unclear cases remain deferred. Fix reference opinions and source packet hashes before any fresh answer. Claim a repeatable selected-case signal only for source-supported wrong cases corrected by the independent model in at least 2/3 draws where the fresh Jev control misses at least 2/3, with B01/P01 maintained; report all regressions, failure, uncertainty and cost first. If Jev baseline fails its own source-backed controls in 2/3 draws, or candidate loses B01/P01 in 2/3, stop and trace. A passing rerun does not erase a stored error. No global quality, calibrated probability, group-rank, or end-to-end claim follows.

**Check controls and mutations:** exercise actual command entry with 54 fake attempts; code paths and variants (bad body SHA, duplicate jobs, bad archive/q, missing input, malformed JSON, duplicate keys, NaN, bad Jev answer set/probabilities, wrong model, DeepSeek truncation/refusal/extra label, 429/reset/timeout, echo secret, launch failure, log failure, mid-batch concurrent failures, blocked worker/deadline, missing usage, pre-existing output directory) must each be deliberately exercised with explicit positive control, judged counts and scratch-only artifacts. Mutate each core check on scratch copy so its negative control goes red. Compare fake-captured outgoing body bytes to registered strings and show exactly one fake invocation per submitted attempt. No real key access allowed in fake controls. Before paid calls run `scripts/preflight.py` with explicitly named completed saved archives/views, read skips and refusals, and independent audit of all request text, standard and schema. If existing preflight cannot cover this clean Step 2 path, state it, and additionally replay the exact archived control identity and saved responses through the current checks at $0; do not infer coverage it does not have. Any semantic judgment is source-reviewed by humans/independent readers, not a new scorer.

## Revision 3: concrete answers to review round 2

**Execution and process death:** replace child processes with one actual OS process containing a fixed pool of at most eight worker threads. The coordinator is the only writer and pre-fsyncs all batch `may_have_been_sent` entries before submitting any worker. A process termination ends all its threads, so no child process can outlive it; the remote provider can still have received a request, and all nonterminal reserved attempts remain unknown, never presumed unsent or unbilled. Each batch has an absolute monotonic deadline `min(global_deadline, batch_start+60)`. Use `concurrent.futures.wait` with that deadline. At deadline, the coordinator persists safe terminal incomplete events for all unfinished jobs and fsyncs, then forcibly terminates its own diagnostic process (`os._exit` in CLI only); OS closes all sockets and stops threads. This does not guarantee a remote request was canceled. If the machine/OS fails before fsync, absence of a terminal marker still means incomplete. A separate subprocess-based fake test kills the *actual coordinator* during blocked fake HTTP, asserts it exits, has no descendant processes, leaves only unknown in-flight records, never resumes, and its test-owned fake server receives no new connections after termination. A socket timeout is defense in depth, not the whole-response deadline. The user authorized this bounded 54-request diagnostic in their latest “开始”; no new approval needed for that same scope.

**Redirect and exact HTTP:** workers use an opener containing an explicit no-redirect handler and one `open` on the fixed official HTTPS endpoint. Statuses in the 3xx range are failures and never followed. The opener cannot delegate to `jev.transport` or default `openai_transport`. A local fake HTTP server captures and counts actual calls, including a 302 with a second target, 429, socket reset and Unicode/key-order cases: exactly one invocation, zero second-target requests, body bytes equal pinned bytes. The coordinator does not send credentials to any URL from a response.

**Bounded response and secret boundary:** reject any declared Content-Length above 2 MiB and read incrementally up to 2 MiB+1. Require full EOF and exact Content-Length when provided; oversize, premature EOF and read errors discard body and fail. With no Content-Length, EOF ends the bounded response; malformed JSON cannot pass. Worker scans raw bytes for credential raw/base64/URL forms, strict parses in memory, then recursively scans every decoded object string, including JSON-unescaped strings, again for all these forms before passing or persisting anything. Error status bodies and all traceback/headers/arbitrary exceptions are always discarded without entering IPC or logs; failure record only enum and numeric status. Successful validated sanitized bodies may be archived, with any serialization after decoded scan also scanned. Fake secrets in raw, JSON escaped, base64 and URL-escaped responses, headers, HTTP error and malformed body must not appear in any file, log or IPC. No real credentials are loaded in fake tests. Provider reported usage JSON is retained with validated safe response; DeepSeek reasoning tokens are a subset of completion tokens, never double-billed. Missing usage is unknown rather than a zero charge.

**Closed provider response contracts:** all JSON parsers reject duplicate object keys, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8. Jev archived validation found 206/206 fresh and 590/590 D392 top-level envelopes exactly `model, answers, usage`, model `jev-1.14.0`; the selected choice answers carry exactly `type, choice, confidence, probabilities`. For this research diagnostic accept only that envelope with model exact, choice field sets exactly as above, real non-bool finite numeric confidence, existing `jev.validate` for every requested question, and `usage` an object; token fields, when present, are non-bool nonnegative integers; missing token fields become unknown. DeepSeek archived validation found 193/193 c8 responses model `deepseek-flash` and standard response metadata; live provider output must be an object with keys from `{id,object,created,model,choices,usage,system_fingerprint}` with required `model,choices`; optional metadata must have their standard types (id/object/fingerprint string or null as appropriate; created integer, not bool; usage object). Require one choice, index zero if present, finish_reason `stop`, message `role=assistant`, non-null string content, refusal absent/null; permit `reasoning_content` string/null and standard optional choice `logprobs`; reject unknown fields in choices or message and any second choice. Strict parse the content, then check the exact three-label schema and reject extra/missing fields. This is a conservative probe contract: actual provider variants that do not match are refusals, never force-fitted. Before paid send positive controls use saved Jev and DeepSeek provider response envelopes (the archive-only `sent_request` field is removed only from the *response control*, never from a request), and a conforming synthetic choice answer. A schema failure in a real previously accepted stored control stops investigation rather than silently loosening validation.

**Evidence chain:** `evidence-chain-DRAFT.json` SHA-256 6b0ab060329917c7bfb7c21648b611f4a856e1c99cac8f43b051c7225ce07146 maps each selected ID to an explicit completed historic archive path and archive SHA, exact full Jev request SHA, original question ID and historic target-answer SHA, source packet/file and incoming/stored source IDs, canonical per-source article SHA, source-opinion and all provider body hashes. `source-pins-DRAFT.json` SHA-256 175a9efa452d1779b6b352e2eee4626acb842a1dcc589e20c1308b0a19422627 pins all 13 complete source and independent-review files. Read no live database; check sqlite URI `mode=ro`, recompute archive file hash before and after archive verification, check `request_json` byte identity and original target answer for each case; fail if archive changes or missing. Explicitly verify the record's quoted passages occur in or are flagged as unverified against corresponding source text; never infer that numerical metadata is supported just by occurrence. Prior source opinions remain provisional and R05 attribution/P01 timing caveats follow the case.

**Result rule:** report each 3-answer row for each arm and every transport/schema/usage failure, no scorer. B01 is expected same and P01 supersedes; each must be selected in >=2/3 fresh Jev-full draws for the diagnostic to support any improvement claim, and >=2/3 independent draws to avoid a repeatable regression. If either fresh Jev-full baseline control fails this condition, stop interpretation and trace. If Jev single and full disagree on a selected relation >=2/3 vs <=1/3, disclose that as request-shape sensitivity and use Jev single for the same-input model comparison, while retaining full results separately; never assign effect solely to model. For B05/B10/H01/R05, a selected-case improvement requires independent correct >=2/3 and fresh Jev-single correct <=1/3 on at least one, with zero repeatable regression on B01/P01; otherwise stop or report inconclusive. One draw does not establish repeatability. P01 only covers direct-denial link, not later forecast changes, and R05 has conflicting party attribution. No global precision/recall, group ranking, model causality or downstream claim.

**Additional fake checks:** include redirect to credential-capturing second server, 2 MiB limit and incomplete Content-Length, all decoded-secret encodings, end-to-end process SIGKILL and timeout with eight blocked fake workers, no orphans, unknown-delivery ledger, no dispatch beyond a failing batch, exclusive scope, source/artifact byte mismatch, no provider-model alias coercion, valid real archived envelope controls, usage absent and invalid. Every check has a positive test and targeted mutant, actual CLI path, judged nonzero sample, no real credentials/services. Preflight baseline run `preflight-v108.log` exited 0 on explicit completed v108 d1: 243 extraction answers; 726 entries judged/12 rejected (7 quote mismatch, 5 duplicate quote); 170 matching judgments, 2 skipped because request absent; 2 earlier schema-refused rows. This matches the earlier score experiment's reported 243/170 and 2 skipped; it does not replay clean Step 2. Explicitly reconstruct and validate all six saved Jev requests and answer shapes separately, plus the selected source/reader opinions; do not claim v108 preflight covers clean Jev or clean c8.

Source-span audit detail: 20 of 21 selected record passages occur byte-for-byte in their saved source article text; R05's stored retailer passage contains a single space where the saved source has a newline between sentences. It matches after collapsing whitespace only. Preserve and report that normalization; do not call it a byte-exact quotation or treat it as a content contradiction. This audit concerns supplied saved source and does not independently validate the upstream article or record attribution.

## Revision 4: eliminate arbitrary retained response text

The diagnostic does not need model reasoning, free-form metadata, IDs, timestamps, provider-generated strings or raw response text. After the raw-byte check, a strict parse, and recursive scanning of all decoded keys and values for the credential and common encodings, the worker returns only a newly constructed **allowlisted structured result**: fixed case/arm/draw identifiers from the manifest; for Jev, the target question ID from the manifest and for every required question only the fixed enum choice and finite numerical confidence/probabilities indexed by the three fixed manifest labels; for DeepSeek, only the fixed enum choice; and for either provider only recognized numeric token usage fields and safe numeric HTTP status. Model `reasoning_content`, generated metadata, arbitrary strings, original content and raw HTTP body are always discarded, even on a successful response. Every retained string is either a fixed local identifier/enum or comes from a fixed question/criterion in the validated request; the serialized allowlist result is checked for credential raw/base64/URL forms before IPC or persistence. Decoded object keys as well as values are scanned. Thus nested JSON or escape sequences in discarded arbitrary response strings can never leave the worker; decoded JSON inside DeepSeek content is itself strict parsed and has only a constrained enum. No arbitrary exception message or error body is retained. Add a fake response with doubly encoded secret in `reasoning_content`, another in response metadata/object keys, and assert no secret or its encoding appears anywhere in IPC, logs or saved files; mutate the allowlist to retain arbitrary fields and prove the test fails. The tradeoff is that raw reasoning and arbitrary successful provider response metadata are not archived; local typed answers, actual input bytes and usage suffice for this probe's comparison, and response refusals are reported only by safe failure type.

## Implementation note: single-process credentials and live-run gate

The coordinator and workers are threads in one process; `main` reads both credentials after the review, preflight and process-state gates and passes them in memory to worker threads. There is no separate worker process or isolated worker address space; the earlier statement that only a child reads keys is superseded. They never enter argv, plan, manifest, event log or fake tests, and safe failure records discard response/error text. Exact key access and gate ordering are subject to the independent sender review. The run-state gate can identify known repository launch commands and repeats immediately before dispatch and every batch; it cannot prove no unrelated process anywhere on the machine makes a paid model call, so the operator also checks known active jobs immediately before send. The complete unmodified v108 preflight output is compared byte-for-byte with the dated baseline, saved alongside the probe, and its two schema-refused, 12 extraction-dropped and two skipped records are disclosed; clean Step 2 still uses the separate six-case stored-answer replay, not that preflight.

The completed D392 stage-2 run is recorded in main commit 9552c8d. For the positive DeepSeek envelope control, a single completed historical archive response was extracted once from d1 segment 2, call_id 1 (source response SHA-256 b44933a35e944cabae3c9bcb43bc8430cc7fa4b43a70906bfcacac21489d4e3e; completed source database SHA-256 e5a182b517ef63431d2501ce8f9268c92f527cf0d71d758efb77e6ef73695005). The archived-only request field was removed and the content replaced with a synthetic three-choice response; free-form reasoning was set to null. The sanitized `deepseek-envelope-control.json` SHA-256 ccce7ed50966b0461a3bb56fc8023481fecc6789ff37631884f7b4a134cf2ec0 is checked directly during dispatch preparation; the live sender does not open that historical trace database.

- Decided, at the owners: `extraction.statement_day` keeps an ISO day and blanks anything else when the answer is sifted (the quote and `event_time` keep the period as written); `writing._store_piece` stores the stated day or '' and the revision path stores the stated day too (the ordering day `new_day` orders the revision only). Readers print the blank; matching's `said_day` still falls back to the publication day for ordering, never for storage. Tests: `test_a_statement_day_is_an_iso_day_or_unknown…` (red on the old sift), `test_an_unknown_statement_day_is_stored_unknown…` (red on the old writer); suite 211; preflight B/C/D unchanged.
- The judge's revision note is labelled as what it is: "Opinion, not verified: the matcher read it as a later version of eX; both are in force" (D202's census: 19 of 37 recorded revisions carry a wrong label).
- Census of the other silent loss in the same path, read pair by pair ([labels](research/2026-10-27-stage34-gold/repeats-40-labels.json)): of 40 sampled `repeat` decisions (1,034 in the run), 32 are pickups, 8 merged a different or richer statement into an old piece and lost its content (an estimated 200 of 1,034). The mechanism is D202's: a one-sample label triggers an irreversible write (a repeat adds a source and discards the incoming text). The fix is the argument record's reader side (store every source record, relate `same_as`, collapse same-claim groups for the judge); not built here.
- D201 measured further ([results](research/2026-10-27-stage34-gold/results.md), 2026-10-28 00:00–01:20, $0.85): a fresh 16-case gold written from the complete expansions before any send (action 11/12 and 4/4 held out; nothing wrongly retired 16/16; same-claim 8/12 with one class: a second outlet's own reporting treated as independent, which the contract could not express); arm 2 split claim identity from source independence (the class is gone; two new judgement weaknesses appeared); three draws per disagreeing case under both prompts show the arm-to-arm differences are within one draw's noise, while in 144 draws no must-not-touch piece was ever marked same or revised. Decided: the contract keeps arm 2's split; prompt arms stop here; the variable fields are annotations under D202 and the next build is the argument record (steps 5 and 6), where a wrong relation in one draw is corrected by the next instead of being frozen into the ledger.

## D204 · 2026-10-28 · A repeat is stored as its own source record; the merge becomes a labelled relation

- Alex: "补那个洞，跑一周验收，仔细思考很重要". The hole (D203's census): on a `repeat` decision the writer adds the incoming item as an outlet of the old piece and discards the incoming text; 8 of 40 sampled repeats (20%, about 200 of 1,034 in the run) had merged a different or richer statement, and its content was gone. The mechanism is D202's: a one-draw label (same_statement ≥ 0.5) triggers an irreversible write.
- Choice weighed. (A) Store the incoming piece, link it to its own destinations, record the pair in `same_claims`, show both to the judge with the relation labelled as the matcher's opinion. (B) Keep the merge and store the text as a variant of the old piece, hidden from the judge. Under (A) true pickups (about 80%) appear twice in view for their first readings, labelled; under (B) the 20% wrong merges stay hidden from the judge. The standard (rule A: an outlet, not a fact; rule C: support counts sources) is served by the label; losing content is the failure that is not recoverable at read time. Decided: (A).
- Decided: `writing` stores every incoming piece once with all its destination links; a `repeat` decision records (target, new, seq) in `same_claims`; the old piece gains no source row and no new link (the new piece carries the outlet and the links; a link written on a one-draw label is a write like any other). `store.evidence_in_force` carries `same_as` (the in-force pieces of its group); the judge's request prints "Opinion, not verified: the matcher read this as the same claim as eX; the argument counts one claim". Readers of `evidence`, `evidence_links` and `evidence_sources` keep their shapes; the library UI's per-row outlet count now counts one row's sources (the claim's outlets are its `same_claims` group), an open UI item.
- Acceptance: tests red on the old writer (`test_a_repeated_statement_is_stored_as_its_own_record…`, the two D167 tests whose assertions pinned the merge, changed with this decision), a mutant that merges again fails them; the 40 sampled repeat decisions replayed through the new writer at $0 (40/40 stored, relation recorded, the 8 lost contents present); then one week through the whole path (`english-v34c-nvda-week`), counting `same_claims` rows, pairs both in the judge's view, and judgements citing both members of a pair (the double-count exposure the label must hold).
- Accepted ([results](research/2026-10-27-stage34-gold/results.md)): 40 of 40 sampled repeat decisions replayed through the new writer keep the piece, the relation and both pieces in force (the 8 lost contents are present); the week through the whole path ran with none failed at $0.23, wrote 45 same-claim relations and no merge, and the judge's reasons where a pair was in view treat the relays as one source ("ultimately trace to SemiAnalysis", "not independent confirmation"). The three-month run may resume on `poc-v34` with D202–D204 in the writer; that is Alex's call.

## 13. Step 2 prompt: Jev working draft

**Purpose:** let a reader inspect the proposed comparison instructions after semantic search has selected candidate evidence. This is a draft for the clean architecture, not the current Jev request or a validated Jev API payload. Response format, score handling, uncertainty and multi-candidate resolution remain open.

**Existing interface:** Jev uses a typed `choice` question and returns a choice with probabilities, not a generated explanation. The current evidence criteria are `same_statement`, `supersedes` and `different`, asked for each selected evidence candidate. `cannot_tell` exists in the current **thesis** relation criteria, not in the evidence criteria. The prose below describes the intended comparison; it still needs to be translated into and tested as an actual Jev request. How to use probabilities and resolve several candidates remains open. [Jev evidence criteria](../src/hivemind/views/jev_matching.py) and [transport](../src/hivemind/jev.py).

**Repeat decision:** `same_statement` is the comparison needed for Alex's chosen repeat behavior. The application must retain which existing evidence candidate produced that result so Step 3 can reuse it, add the incoming source and create any missing thesis link. A similar topic or number alone is not enough to establish a repeat. This is a clean-design requirement, not a claim that the current writer already does it.

### What Jev receives

- The thesis the incoming evidence is proposed for.
- The incoming evidence, including its available source, speaker and stated time.
- A candidate prior evidence record returned from the entity-wide search, with its available context; it may be linked to another thesis.
- The comparison instructions and the three relationship descriptions below. The diagram specifies the outcomes; how comparisons are batched is not yet decided.

### Proposed comparison instruction

```text
Compare the incoming evidence with the candidate existing evidence for the entity.
Use the supplied statements and their available source, speaker and time.

Determine which relationship best describes the two statements:

REPEAT: The incoming statement presents the same claim again, including a
retelling or another source reporting that claim.

REVISION: The incoming statement is a later account that changes the same
earlier statement, such as a revised forecast or an updated statement by its
source. Merely being later or about the same subject is not enough.

DIFFERENT: The statements describe different facts, claims or periods rather
than a repeat or revision of the same claim. Distinct original claimants can
make separate claims; a different reporting source may simply retell one.

Consider the wording, figures, speaker, original source, what each statement
refers to, and when it was stated. Similar wording or the same figure alone
does not prove the statements are the same. Do not infer missing details.
Identify the relationship and the existing evidence being compared. If the
supplied information does not establish a relationship, express uncertainty.
```

### Input to be inserted at runtime

```text
[Thesis]
<thesis identity and description>

[Incoming evidence]
<statement and available source, speaker and time>

[Existing evidence]
<one search result and its available source, speaker and time>
```

Jev's pairwise `DIFFERENT` outcome is not proof that no other record in the library matches. Search selection, N, confidence thresholds, the representation and handling of uncertainty, and the rule for combining multiple comparisons are open; this draft does not specify a forced choice when the information is insufficient.

## 14. Existing components to reference during the rebuild

The intended starting point is the existing thesis and evidence database. This map identifies the repository components corresponding to the diagram so they can be inspected and selectively reused. A link identifies existing code or data; it does not mean that the component already implements the clean design or that it should be copied unchanged.

3	2026-11-09: Alex authorized source review of all 56 saved D392 clean-d1 Step 2 candidate answers labeled supersedes, plus two blinded source readers and true revision control. The population is all such answers, not 56 independent incoming articles. `build_packet.py` reads the completed run and its completed predecessor in SQLite read-only mode. It resolves exact incoming IDs, actual compared original group records, complete source IDs, actual outputs and all group links. Preconditions: 56 answers, each linked in the saved outcome; 34 distinct incoming records; record IDs unique; source text is identical if present in both segments; all source IDs found; earlier original record precedes incoming article; known R05 pair 203:e1 → 119:e1 is present. Every source quotation (236 passages in all 76 pairs) is present in its saved complete article under whitespace normalization. Source article order is not proof of the time of the original claim or response.

The saved library consolidates repeated links between the same two groups: 30 retain the particular incoming record as their `by` field and 26 correspond to an already-present group link attributed to another incoming record. Every one of the 56 has its destination group represented, but they are not 56 separately stored edges. 20 sampled other-choice candidate comparisons are mixed and shuffled as controls, so the blind readers cannot infer any specific original Jev answer from case inclusion. Controls are not representative and have not been source-adjudicated in advance. The key identifies candidate outcomes and is not shown to the readers. A fixed seed 20261109 determines the sample and shuffle, and six packet SHA-256 hashes are printed by the builder. Source readers independently receive the same 76 source-only pairs, the present PRD definition, and which record fields Jev did or did not see, without receiving historic choices or other reader answers.
